title: Initial objects and monomorphisms
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a category. An object $I$ of $\mathcal C$ is *initial* if for every object $Y$ of $\mathcal C$ there is exactly one morphism $I\to Y$; equivalently, $I$ is a colimit of the empty diagram (the empty coproduct). A morphism $f:X\to Y$ of $\mathcal C$ is a *monomorphism* if for every object $W$ and every pair of morphisms $a,b:W\to X$ with $f\circ a=f\circ b$ one has $a=b$.
